Subject: Re: Intro — Redwood dedicated eval

Rishi,

Thanks for last week's demo. The engineering team loved the latency profile, and procurement asked me to get something in writing about the steps to close and what triggers pricing changes. We've talked internally about a ramped commitment rather than an all-in reservation. Can you send a mutual action plan (MAP) that maps evaluation milestones to committed GPU capacity, pricing tiers, and burst allowance?

High level asks from our side:
- Short EVAL period (4 weeks) with a production-like load test in week 3
- If eval passes, commit to a 12-month pool with a 3-stage ramp (30% -> 60% -> 100%)
- Clear burst policy for spikes (how many GPUs, duration, and overage rates)
- Any discounting tied to term length / payment cadence

Can you include details on billing start (upon commit vs. upon capacity delivery) and any SLA credits for latency/uptime?

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of AI Platforms | Aperture Labs

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & commitment staircase — Aperture Labs Dedicated eval + burst terms

Elena — great to hear the demo resonated. Attached is a draft MAP and a GPU sizing worksheet to make the ramp concrete. Key points up front: current proposal is a 4-week evaluation (no charge for baseline trial tokens), production-like soak in week 3, then a 12-month committed pool with a staircase commit at day 30 and day 90. Pricing tiers and burst are summarized below.

Summary (high level):
- Eval: 4 weeks; engineering validation; Redwood provides a dedicated test pool with limited preemption
- Commit structure: 12 months; staged baseline commit 30% at sign, 60% at month 2, 100% at month 4
- Burst policy: 50% additional GPUs available for 6 hours/day at 1.5x unit rate; emergency burst (up to 100% additional) at 2.5x unit rate with 24-48h notice
- Billing: billing for committed capacity begins on provisioning date for the committed pool; credits if we miss provisioning SLA
- Discounts: 12-month term standard discount 12%; prepayment (annual) additional 3%

Attachments: MAP_Aperture_v1.2.pdf, GPU-sizing-sheet.xlsx, Redwood-Dedicated-Terms-2026.pdf

Next steps: 1) confirm evaluation start date (we can start as early as Nov 2), 2) aperture shares production load profile & expected peak tokens/day, 3) procurement reviews attached terms. Vanessa, can you confirm whether the burst durations above align with capacity planning?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Elena / Rishi — quick read-through from capacity planning. A few clarifications:
- The "50% additional GPUs" burst is expressed relative to the baseline committed pool; we'll cap concurrent burst instances to 24 GPUs unless you need larger bursts and sign a short-term addendum.
- Emergency burst (100% additional) requires a 24-hour notice for warm-up; we can support same-day emergency bursts if the cluster has idle capacity, but that's not guaranteed.
- We can instrument a soft-prefetch cache for your test workload during the eval soak to reduce cold-start token costs.

Suggested change to MAP: include acceptance criteria for the week-3 soak (p95 latency < 250ms for text-gen baseline, error rate < 0.5%). If criteria met, the first staircase payment and provisioning kicks at day 30. If not met, we propose a 2-week remediation and retest window.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Capacity Ops | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & commitment staircase — Aperture Labs Dedicated eval + burst terms

Thanks — this is getting us close. A couple of procurement asks:
- Can you expose the per-GPU unit price (USD/hr) for committed tier vs burst so we can model TCO?
- Can you confirm whether billing start could be 'upon sign' with a 30-day provisioning SLA instead of 'upon provisioning' — procurement prefers to align the contract term to the signature date. If you can offer a 30-day provisioning SLA with an SLA credit of 5% for each week late (capped at 20%), that would be acceptable.

Also, we're sensitive to the staircase timing: our infra budget is allocated quarterly, so can we move the 2nd step to month 3 instead of month 2? That gives us runway to reallocate if internal approvals slip.

Elena
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & commitment staircase — Aperture Labs Dedicated eval + burst terms

Elena — appreciate the constructive feedback. Quick answers and an updated path forward below. Full redline will go to procurement by EOD; I'm attaching a short pricing table in the MAP for clarity.

Responses: 
- Per-GPU pricing (committed baseline): $2.80 / GPU-hour; burst (50% additional) at $4.20 / GPU-hour; emergency burst at $7.00 / GPU-hour (short-term addendum required)
- Billing start: we can accept 'billing start upon signature' with a 30-day provisioning SLA and the SLA credit language you proposed (5% per week late, cap 20%)
- Staircase timing: we can move the 2nd step to month 3 (30% -> 60% at month 3 -> 100% at month 5) to accommodate your quarterly budget cycles
- Acceptance criteria: we'll include the week-3 soak pass/fail thresholds as Vanessa suggested; remediation window of 14 days included

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll send the redline to procurement (DocuSign-ready) by EOD today;
2) If procurement approves the redline, we sign and target Nov 2 start for the eval (we can still flip the start if you prefer November 9);
3) Vanessa to schedule a capacity warm-up run during eval week 3;
4) Rishi/Neha to run a short pricing sensitivity model for Aperture's expected peak tokens/day.

Thanks all — leaning toward a Nov eval start.

Best,
Rishi
